blocks.text:
Breakfast at the hotel.

Quito city tour and Rucu Pichincha Volcano.

The sightseeing day, including transfers, lasts 8 hours.

Altitude: 2,800–4,100 m.

Average temperature: +10–20°C during the day and +10°C at night.

During the city tour of Quito, you will see panoramic views, churches, domes and rooftops that form part of its historic heritage, and learn about colonial art, architecture, culture, legends and traditions.

Quito, the capital of Ecuador, was founded in the 16th century on the ruins of an Inca city and stands at an altitude of 2,800 m. Despite the earthquake of 1917, it has the best-preserved and least-altered historic centre in Latin America. Its architecture and rich interiors are examples of the Quito School of Art, which combines Spanish, Italian, Moorish, Flemish and Indigenous artistic traditions. Artists of this school worked in stone and wood to depict major religious events. After an hour and a half exploring the Old Town on foot, you will understand why Quito was the first city in the world to be included on UNESCO's cultural heritage list.

Quito takes its name from the Quitu people, who inhabited the region long before the Spanish conquest. In 1533, Sebastián de Benalcázar took control of the city, which had previously been a capital of the Inca Empire, and in 1541 it was granted the status of a Spanish city. Its full name is San Francisco de Quito. The city was the capital of the State of Quito until the end of Spanish colonial rule.

The Franciscans were the first religious order to establish themselves in Quito. They immediately began building a monastery that became a centre of education and art, with its own schools of painting and sculpture.

The country's principal buildings surround the main square, Plaza Grande: the Cathedral, the Presidential Palace, the Archbishop's Palace and City Hall. We will visit one of the city's finest examples of colonial art, the Jesuit church with its intricately carved facade.

We will also visit the Gothic Basílica del Voto Nacional.

This religious building was designed by a French architect inspired by Notre-Dame de Paris. The Basilica of the National Vow is considered the country's most representative work of neo-Gothic architecture and one of the most outstanding in Latin America.

Founded in the 19th century, the basilica is considered unfinished. Its facade features gargoyles and animals native to the country and region, including caimans, tortoises, boobies and monkeys.

The church measures 140 m in length and 35 m in width, with a central nave 30 m high.

Its two front towers rise to 115 m. The basilica is one of the tallest buildings in the city.

Quito is a capital of many contrasts, which you can appreciate by visiting both the Old Town and the newer districts.

From the El Panecillo viewpoint, with its statue of the winged Virgin Mary, the city's patron saint, you will have a beautiful view across Quito.

At midday, we continue towards Rucu Pichincha Volcano.

Transfer to the TelefériQo cable car. A ride up to its viewpoint is an excellent way to appreciate Quito's setting among the Andes.

The ascent takes 20 minutes, starting at 2,950 m and reaching 4,100 m over a distance of 2.5 km. From the viewpoint, you can see almost the entire city.

We will ascend to the top of Cruz Loma hill and take a short walk through the páramo, the high-altitude ecosystem of the Andes. This short hike offers beautiful views of Ecuador's capital and the surrounding volcanoes. In clear weather, we may see Cotopaxi, Antisana, Cayambe and others.

A box lunch is included.

Stops: Basílica del Voto Nacional, the main square, the Golden Church, San Francisco Square, the hill with the Virgin Mary statue and the cable car.

Accommodation at Patio Andaluz 4*: www.hotelpatioandaluz.com

(Breakfast, box lunch)
